references.text: Heshbon is mentioned as a city the Israelites captured from Sihon, king of the Amorites, and which was given to the tribe of Reuben.
Heshbon and Dibon are among the cities that the sons of Gad and Reuben wanted to settle in on the east side of the Jordan.
Nebo and Baal-Meon are mentioned as cities that the sons of Reuben rebuilt, and Baal-Meon received a new name.
Dibon-Gad is mentioned as a campsite for the Israelites during their wilderness journey.
Heshbon and Dibon are mentioned in the prophecy against Moab, highlighting the significance of these cities in the region.
Dibon is mentioned in Jeremiah's judgment against Moab.
Beth-Baal-Meon is listed among the cities in Moab that will be struck by judgment.
Beth-Baal-Meon is mentioned as one of Moab's border cities in Ezekiel's prophecy.
